html:
The map's name, in its 1880 snapshot, for the Muslim sultanate of Wadai, east of Lake Chad in what is now Chad. Its earlier history is told under Wadai Sultanate.

In the second half of the 1800s Wadai was the strongest state of the central Sudan. Sultan Ali, who ruled from 1858 to 1874, built up its wealth from the capital at Abeche. Its caravans crossed the Sahara north to Benghazi through the oases of the Senussi religious order, carrying slaves and ivory raided from the lands to the south. Wadai dominated its western neighbour Bagirmi and rivalled Darfur.

In the 1890s the warlord Rabih az-Zubayr threatened it from the south. The French arrived after Rabih fell. They took Abeche in 1909, and Wadai resistance ended by 1912.
